# Replication: Weiß and Kim (2024)

This page reproduces **Table B.8** of @weiss2024b. The table reports simulated rejection
rates of the four asymptotic spatial ordinal pattern (SOP) tests at level
$\alpha = 0.05$, together with the spatial autocorrelation at lag $\mathbf{1}$ as a
benchmark, for DGP 8 and growing field size.

## Libraries

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| message: false
using StatsOrdinalPatterns, Random, Statistics, Printf, DataFrames, Distributions
```

## Statistics of the paper and their types in the package

Each column of Table B.8 corresponds to one `chart_choice` of [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd), which returns
the statistic, the asymptotic critical value, the $p$ value and the reject decision. The
benchmark column is [`test_sacf`](../reference/test_sacf.qmd).

| Table B.8 column | Package call | Rejects $H_0$ when | Label below |
|:-----------------|:-------------|:-------------------|:------------|
| $\hat{\tau}$ | [`test_sop(data, 1, 1; chart_choice=TauHat())`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) | $\lvert\hat{\tau}\rvert > c$ | `tau_hat` |
| $\hat{\kappa}$ | [`test_sop(data, 1, 1; chart_choice=KappaHat())`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) | $\lvert\hat{\kappa}\rvert > c$ | `kappa_hat` |
| $\tilde{\tau}$ | [`test_sop(data, 1, 1; chart_choice=TauTilde())`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) | $\lvert\tilde{\tau}\rvert > c$ | `tau_tilde` |
| $\tilde{\kappa}$ | [`test_sop(data, 1, 1; chart_choice=KappaTilde())`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) | $\lvert\tilde{\kappa}\rvert > c$ | `kappa_tilde` |
| $\hat{\rho}(\mathbf{1})$ | [`test_sacf(data, 1, 1)`](../reference/test_sacf.qmd) | $\lvert\hat{\rho}\rvert > c$ | `rho_1` |

All four SOP statistics are linear in the same vector of type frequencies
$\hat{\mathbf{p}} = (\hat p_1, \hat p_2, \hat p_3)$ of the classical SOP classification,
which [`stat_sop`](../reference/stat_sop.qmd) returns as its second output.

The header of the table asks for critical values computed with the exact variance.
[`crit_val_sop`](../reference/crit_val_sop.qmd) uses exactly that: its variances carry the finite sample factor
$1 - 1/(2m) - 1/(2n)$, so no asymptotic simplification enters the critical values below.

## Setup

DGP 8 is the spatial quadratic moving average process SQMA(1,1) with
$(\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3) = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)$ and i.i.d. standard normal errors. The
[`SQMA11`](../reference/SQMA11.qmd) type of the package holds it: `dgp_params` are the $\beta_j$, `eps_params` are
the exponents $(a, b, c)$ of the three error terms, written "$1^a\,2^b\,3^c$" in the
paper, and `M_rows`, `N_cols` are the dimensions of the simulated field.

`m` and `n` in the table are the dimensions of the SOP matrix, so the field is
$(m+1) \times (n+1)$.

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Parameters of Table B.8 and one field of DGP 8"
β = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)                                # dependence parameters of Table B.8
level = 0.05                                       # nominal significance level
sizes = ((10, 10), (15, 15), (20, 20), (40, 25))   # SOP matrix dimensions (m, n)
reps = 10_000                                      # Monte Carlo replications

models = [
    ("DGP8-1", "1² 2² 3²", (2, 2, 2)),
    ("DGP8-2", "1² 2¹ 3²", (2, 1, 2)),
    ("DGP8-3", "1¹ 2¹ 3²", (1, 1, 2)),
    ("DGP8-4", "1² 2¹ 3¹", (2, 1, 1)),
]

charts = [
    ("tau_hat", TauHat()),
    ("kappa_hat", KappaHat()),
    ("tau_tilde", TauTilde()),
    ("kappa_tilde", KappaTilde()),
]

# One field of the DGP. `fill_mat_dgp_sop!` is the routine the ARL functions of the
# package use internally; it writes into the caller's buffers and returns a view of the
# field. `mat` receives the field, `mat_ma` the errors, `mat_ao` the additive outliers,
# which DGP 8 does not have.
sqma11(eps, m, n) = SQMA11(β, eps, m + 1, n + 1, Normal(0, 1), nothing)

buffers(dgp) = ntuple(_ -> zeros(dgp.M_rows + 1, dgp.N_cols + 1), 3)

draw_field!(dgp, mat, mat_ao, mat_ma) =
    StatsOrdinalPatterns.fill_mat_dgp_sop!(dgp, dgp.dist, dgp.dist_ao, mat, mat_ao, mat_ma)
```

## A single test

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "One field of DGP 8 and one SOP test"
Random.seed!(1)
dgp = sqma11((2, 2, 2), 10, 10)
Y = collect(draw_field!(dgp, buffers(dgp)...))   # copy out of the buffer
test_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=TauTilde(), alpha=level)
```

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "The SACF benchmark on the same field"
test_sacf(Y, 1, 1; alpha=level)
```

## Running the power study

[`crit_val_sop`](../reference/crit_val_sop.qmd) and [`crit_val_sacf`](../reference/crit_val_sacf.qmd) return the critical values alone. They depend on the
field size and the level, not on the data, so they are computed once per row of the table.
[`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) additionally computes the $p$ value, which a power study does not use. Each
replication then costs one pass over the field: [`stat_sop`](../reference/stat_sop.qmd) counts the SOP frequencies
once, and the four statistics are read off the resulting $\hat{\mathbf{p}}$ with
[`chart_stat_sop`](../reference/chart_stat_sop.qmd).

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Rejection rates of the five tests for one field size"
function power(m, n, eps, reps; level=0.05)
    dgp = sqma11(eps, m, n)
    M, N = dgp.M_rows, dgp.N_cols
    crits = [crit_val_sop(M, N, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, alpha=level) for (_, cc) in charts]
    crit_rho = crit_val_sacf(M, N; alpha=level)

    tasks = map(Iterators.partition(1:reps, cld(reps, Threads.nthreads()))) do idx
        Threads.@spawn begin
            bufs = buffers(dgp)                     # one set of buffers per task
            hits = zeros(Int, length(charts) + 1)
            for _ in idx
                Y = draw_field!(dgp, bufs...)
                p̂ = stat_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)))[2]
                for (j, (_, cc)) in enumerate(charts)
                    hits[j] += abs(chart_stat_sop(p̂, cc)) > crits[j]
                end
                hits[end] += abs(stat_sacf(Y, 1, 1)) > crit_rho
            end
            hits
        end
    end
    return sum(fetch.(tasks)) ./ reps
end
```

The shortcut has to give the same statistic and the same decision as [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) and
[`test_sacf`](../reference/test_sacf.qmd), not merely a similar one:

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Check against test_sop and test_sacf"
let dgp = sqma11((1, 1, 2), 20, 20), M = 21, N = 21
    Y = collect(draw_field!(dgp, buffers(dgp)...))   # copy out of the buffer
    p̂ = stat_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)))[2]
    ok = all(
        begin
            r = test_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, alpha=level)
            s = chart_stat_sop(p̂, cc)
            s ≈ r.stat && crit_val_sop(M, N, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, alpha=level) ≈ r.asymp_crit &&
                (abs(s) > r.asymp_crit) == r.asymp_reject
        end for (_, cc) in charts
    )
    ok &= (abs(stat_sacf(Y, 1, 1)) > crit_val_sacf(M, N; alpha=level)) ==
          test_sacf(Y, 1, 1; alpha=level).asymp_reject
    (shortcut_matches_test_sop=ok,)
end
```

::: {.callout-note}
With `reps = 10_000` the page runs in a few seconds and the standard error of a rejection
rate is at most $\sqrt{0.25 / 10^4} = 0.005$.
:::

## Table B.8: DGP 8, $(\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3) = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)$

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Run the study for every model and field size"
res = Dict(
    (name, m, n) => power(m, n, eps, reps; level=level)
    for (name, _, eps) in models for (m, n) in sizes
)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
tab = DataFrame(
    model=[name for (name, _, _) in models for _ in sizes],
    label=[lab for (_, lab, _) in models for _ in sizes],
    m=[m for _ in models for (m, _) in sizes],
    n=[n for _ in models for (_, n) in sizes],
)
for (j, (nm, _)) in enumerate(charts)
    tab[!, nm] = [round(res[(name, m, n)][j], digits=3) for (name, _, _) in models for (m, n) in sizes]
end
tab[!, "rho_1"] = [round(res[(name, m, n)][end], digits=3) for (name, _, _) in models for (m, n) in sizes]
tab
```

The paper prints the maximal rejection rate of each row in bold:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
stats = vcat([nm for (nm, _) in charts], "rho_1")
maxima = [maximum(tab[i, s] for s in stats) for i in 1:nrow(tab)]
DataFrame(
    model=tab.model, m=tab.m, n=tab.n,
    max_stat=[join([s for s in stats if tab[i, s] == maxima[i]], ", ") for i in 1:nrow(tab)],
    rate=maxima,
)
```

### Comparison with the published rates

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# published values, ordered (tau_hat, kappa_hat, tau_tilde, kappa_tilde, rho_1)
published = Dict(
    ("DGP8-1", 10, 10) => (0.142, 0.160, 0.249, 0.061, 0.069),
    ("DGP8-1", 15, 15) => (0.216, 0.361, 0.476, 0.069, 0.088),
    ("DGP8-1", 20, 20) => (0.357, 0.581, 0.769, 0.064, 0.097),
    ("DGP8-1", 40, 25) => (0.713, 0.929, 0.989, 0.076, 0.112),
    ("DGP8-2", 10, 10) => (0.246, 0.403, 0.589, 0.072, 0.082),
    ("DGP8-2", 15, 15) => (0.422, 0.809, 0.919, 0.075, 0.103),
    ("DGP8-2", 20, 20) => (0.654, 0.968, 0.997, 0.066, 0.118),
    ("DGP8-2", 40, 25) => (0.959, 1.000, 1.000, 0.076, 0.128),
    ("DGP8-3", 10, 10) => (0.268, 0.195, 0.382, 0.088, 0.079),
    ("DGP8-3", 15, 15) => (0.455, 0.457, 0.703, 0.121, 0.100),
    ("DGP8-3", 20, 20) => (0.708, 0.706, 0.945, 0.154, 0.105),
    ("DGP8-3", 40, 25) => (0.976, 0.982, 1.000, 0.296, 0.116),
    ("DGP8-4", 10, 10) => (0.156, 0.131, 0.215, 0.069, 0.474),
    ("DGP8-4", 15, 15) => (0.246, 0.286, 0.412, 0.080, 0.882),
    ("DGP8-4", 20, 20) => (0.392, 0.457, 0.688, 0.085, 0.992),
    ("DGP8-4", 40, 25) => (0.755, 0.846, 0.974, 0.130, 1.000),
)

cmp = DataFrame(model=String[], m=Int[], n=Int[], statistic=String[],
    paper=Float64[], replicated=Float64[], dev=Float64[])
for (name, _, _) in models, (m, n) in sizes, (j, nm) in enumerate(stats)
    r = res[(name, m, n)][j]
    push!(cmp, (name, m, n, nm, published[(name, m, n)][j], round(r, digits=3),
        round(r - published[(name, m, n)][j], digits=3)))
end
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
@printf("largest absolute deviation: %.3f\n", maximum(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("mean absolute deviation:    %.3f\n", mean(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("Monte Carlo standard error: at most %.3f\n", sqrt(0.25 / reps))
```

The five largest deviations across all 80 entries:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
first(sort(cmp, :dev, by=abs, rev=true), 5)
```
